dedupe_keys.name: spatially distributed freshwater demand for electricity in africa 2 534 power plants with cooling water withdrawal and consumption 2020

description: This database from the International Water Management Institute (IWMI), built under the CGIAR Initiative on Foresight, estimates the freshwater demand of electricity production in Africa for 2020. It covers 2,534 power plants, classed by fuel type, operation cycle, infrastructure, cooling system and local climate, and gives for each plant its installed capacity, electricity generated in 2020, coordinates and the type of cooling water used, per fuel type and country. Total withdrawal and consumption were estimated at 33,108 and 23,822 million cubic metres a year, with results at national, subnational and river basin levels. Plant data were compiled from the GEM Wiki, Power Technology, Google Maps, national reports and newspapers, combined with water use factors by plant type and cooling technology and Köppen-Geiger climate zones; country totals were checked against IEA 2020 data, or IRENA 2021 data for small countries. Coverage: Africa, 2020. Format and access: two Excel files in the supporting information of the paper in Environmental Science: Water Research & Technology (doi:10.1039/D4EW00246F), linked from the IWMI data page; free, open access. Licence (read on 2026-09-29): IWMI terms of use: reuse with attribution for non-commercial, research or educational purposes, share-alike. Caveats: water use is estimated from factors, not measured, and the Excel files were not opened. Simulation uses: power plant locations with cooling water demand for energy-water interdependency and drought or heat stress studies of generation. Related records: the Global Power Plant Database (data-global-power-plant-database) and the GEM Global Integrated Power Tracker (data-gem-global-integrated-power-tracker).
